messages:
lena.q: Heads up, hitting a weird gap where plaintext pino logs show req_id=<redacted> but the JSON output in the same run contains req_id. Happens with LOG_LEVEL=debug + OTEL_LOG_HOOK=1 in sampleapp.

lena.q: Repro (local):
```bash
git checkout sampleapp@v0.12.3
export REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=otel
export OTEL_LOG_HOOK=1
export LOG_LEVEL=debug
node examples/sampleapp.js &
# send a request that triggers auth retry/backoff
curl -s http://localhost:8000/api/long-poll
```

lena.q: Example lines from same process (stdout):
`[2025-10-05T12:03:10.123Z] DEBUG auth.retry attempt=2 user=bob - req_id=<redacted>`
and the structured logger line: `{"ts":"2025-10-05T12:03:10.123Z","level":"debug","msg":"auth.retry","req_id":"r-9b2c","attempt":2}`

lena.q: Intermittent and seems correlated with retries/backoff. When LOG_LEVEL=info it's much rarer.

rob_sdk: Which node version and @redwood/telemetry-sdk version? Also are we using pino hooks or a custom transform for plaintext formatting?

lena.q: Node 16 in my repro, sdk 0.21.4, pino v7. Plaintext is our human formatter that reads a meta field captured when logger was created.

mike_o: Likely ordering/context issue. If the plaintext formatter captures req_id at logger construction time (or during an earlier sync event) and OTEL hook restores context asynchronously on retry callbacks, you'll see a mismatch. Structured JSON path often reads fields at write time and can call into context correctly, while legacy formatters may not.

vlad: Agreed. We've seen similar with setImmediate + async_hooks races during auth backoff. Node async_hooks can drop context when code crosses a timer boundary if the hook restoring the trace context happens after the formatter has already prepared the line.

lena.q: I tried two quick toggles: initTelemetry() before logger creation — issue went away in my runs. Creating logger first then telemetry reproduce rate ~60-80% for that scenario.

rob_sdk: Good catch. That indicates our sampleapp starter needs to recommend telemetry init before logger and we should update the OTEL_LOG_HOOK docs.

mike_o: Short-term workaround for users who can't reorder: change the plaintext formatter to read req_id from telemetry at serialize/write time instead of capturing it in closure. Example: 
```js
// naive: captures at creation time -> broken on reorder
const logger = pino({ prettyPrint: { formatter: () => ({ req_id: telemetry.getReqId() }) }});
// better: patch logMethod to inject req_id at call time
const logger2 = pino({ hooks: { logMethod (args, method) { args[0] = Object.assign({}, args[0], { req_id: telemetry.getReqId() }); method.apply(this, args); }}});
```

lena.q: Will file a small PR to sampleapp (docs + reorder example) and add an integration test that runs with OTEL_LOG_HOOK=1 + LOG_LEVEL=debug to verify retries keep req_id present.

rob_sdk: Please include a test matrix for node 14/16/18 and simulate a backoff (setTimeout wraps) so we catch async_hooks oddities. Also add a note in SDK parity doc noting python/coroutines vs node/async_hooks behavior.

ci-bot: CI TODO: add test job redwood/sampleapp#4382 (queued).

vlad: Long-term we discussed a telemetry persistence env var to force context propagation via async_hooks fallback (REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_PERSIST_CONTEXT=1) or a tiny shim that rebinds timers. That might reduce customer footguns, but it's a heavier lift and can have perf tradeoffs.

rob_sdk: Agreed. We'll prioritize the sampleapp docs + tests and a minor SDK patch to prefer runtime-reading of req_id in our pretty-printers. Create an RFC if we want the env-level shim.

lena.q: Thanks everyone. I'll drop repro logs and the PR link once ready. Appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:
